commits.author: loom-oa-dev[bot]
commits.message:
[zephyr] Keep one idle worker for final-shard retries (#10976)

Keep one idle worker available while a dedicated Zephyr pipeline has
unfinished final-stage shards. Extra idle workers still exit, and the
retained worker exits when the stage completes. This lets it run a shard
requeued after another worker's heartbeat expires.

The November 5 Datakit smoke run stopped at 105/106 quality shards: Iris
retried a worker, its replacement received `SHUTDOWN` while the old
attempt still owned the last shard, and the shard requeued after the
worker job ended. A local coordinator regression reproduced that
ordering before the change and completed the retry afterward. With 106
worker states, the final-stage drain predicate took 4.6 µs per pull
versus 0.6 µs before; the retained worker can occupy one slot for the
remainder of the stage.

The affected coordinator suite passed 81 tests, and the advisory lint
review found no issues. The repository test selector reached 2,167
passes before its 600-second cap; five evaluation-driver tests failed
because this host's Python lacks `os.pidfd_open`. A live ferry has not
run on this branch.

Fixes #10974

Co-authored-by: loom <claude-max-1@openathena.ai>

commits.author: mcwitt
commits.message:
[eval] Exclude tags with no scored tokens from eval macros (#11054)

Eval macros and per-tag logs now skip tags with no scored tokens, with a
warning for each unscored leaf tag. At 262K, `ptb` and `wikitext_103`
are shorter than one sequence, so they logged a loss of 0 and
`eval_dropless/macro_loss` averaged those zeros in.
`eval_dropless/paloma/macro_loss` already excluded them. A parent tag
whose children are all unscored is also skipped, where `np.average`
previously raised `ZeroDivisionError`.

The macros are computed from the host arrays after the eval loop, so
`accum_for_batch`, training and compiled programs are unchanged. The
macro's two eager `jnp.mean` calls are gone and no device operation
replaces them.

On a run with no empty tag, the macro stays a float32 average and only
the summation order changes: over 2000 random trials at 8 to 100 tags it
moved by at most 7.2e-7. At 262K, `eval_dropless/macro_loss` rises by
16/14 to about 2.05, so the canary's eval row compares against a
baseline that mixes both values until earlier runs age out. That row
only feeds the 2.5 ceiling; the Slack regression post uses step time.

Taken from #10711. Its padded final windows, which would score these two
sets, remain separate, so these tags stay unlogged until that lands.
Part of #8435.

commits.author: mcwitt
commits.message:
[grug] Train the hero at 262K from the merged step-390251 checkpoint (#11041)

The hero trains at 262,144-token context from a merged checkpoint at step 390251, with CP4 x EP16 and batch 176 on 11 racks. It stops at step 393491, 3,240 steps and 149.5B tokens past the schedule. The learning rate moves from 5% to 1% of peak.

- Start: [`hero-ctx65k-merge-hb-avg11/step-390251`](https://filer.marina.oa.dev/#s3%3A%2F%2Fmarin-us-east-02a%2Fmarin%2Fgrug%2Fhero-ctx65k-merge-hb-avg11%2Fcheckpoints%2Fstep-390251) is an equal-weight hyperball average of the parent's last 11 permanent checkpoints. `hero_checkpoint_paths` reads the parent from the W&B fork, because a merged path names no run.
- Recipe: global 1.84, from `qk_mult` 1.66 and `qk_mult_long_scale` 1.108. Global layers only, because the no-training sweep at step-390251 had lower real-text loss at the same value: 0.0024 lower than all-layers 1.84 at 262K, on all 19 subsets, with recovery 0.933 against 0.938 (intervals overlap). See the [notebook](https://github.com/marin-community/marin-logbooks/blob/e1f35f7dcbd0f1a5da4f9dac3ccc2c425af06cf4/logbooks/37-hero-262k/notebook.md) and [issue](https://github.com/marin-community/marin-logbooks/issues/37).
- Finalists: first of two. The second depends on #10986, starts from the same checkpoint on a branch, and merges next Monday only if it wins.
- Data: the hero reads the long-context mix. The train loader queues 64 batches instead of 512. #10994 prevents the eval memory failure at 262K.
- Saves: seven permanent checkpoints, about 30 TB.

Evidence limits:

- No training run tested global 1.84, and no rehearsal ran. This head has not trained on GPU.
- The arms, such as [global 1.88](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe/runs/hero-lce11-merged-global188), ran interim code. This head adds #10556, which reading `api.py:92` and a CPU check with stand-in kernels show is inert for hero training. Nobody checked GB200 compiled code.
- We inferred memory from a [queue-64 run](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe/runs/hero-lce11-q64-log65536sq) of another recipe. All six queue-512 recipes read 182.22 GiB. The hero's first reading tests 180.44 GiB.
- The `eval_regressed` alert should fire on the first two evals, from partial windows that #10711 fixes. We inferred this from the [alert rule](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/docs/ops/hero-run-health-alerts.md). No run showed it.

This merges after #10917.

Part of #8435.

commits.author: mcwitt
commits.message:
[grug] Let the hero train past its schedule (#10917)

The hero can train past its 390251-step schedule through a checked-in `HERO_SCHEDULE_EXTENSION`.

- The value is `None`, so the live run stops at 390251. A deploy PR sets `ScheduleExtension(steps=N, final_lr_ratio=R)`.
- `num_train_steps` stays 390251. A larger value changes learning rates, epsilon, weight-decay anneal, and context-phase replay.
- Past 390251, both optimizer groups move linearly from 5% of peak to `R` of peak over `N` steps. The config rejects `R` outside 0 to 5%.
- Rates through 390251 are bitwise identical. Weight decay stays 0, data stays on cooldown weights, and permanent checkpoints continue every 500 steps.
- A stop past the schedule without a sufficient extension raises at config build. It was silently capped. A restore past the stop step raises.
- The final checkpoint comes before the forced end-of-run callbacks, so a failed final eval cannot lose it.
- A retry that restores a permanent stop-step checkpoint logs `ZERO-STEP SUCCESS`, skips callbacks and save, and succeeds. A missing final eval must run offline. Without the skip, each retry repeats the eval and adds several TB to OCDBT.
- Restoring a temporary stop-step checkpoint saves and runs callbacks.
- Periodic evals, including one at the stop step, run before their step's checkpoint.
- A rehearsal needs a branch that sets `HERO_SCHEDULE_EXTENSION` and runs at the rack's own rates.
- CPU loop tests use SGD; another checkpoints the real optimizer into the extension.
- GPU rehearsals used 3544ec8e04, which also had `--extension-*`, `--optimizer-racks`, and an earlier stop-step save. This PR lacks them. Those runs trained 262K from 390251 to 390351. A retry left step-390351 byte-identical. A 5-step resume wrote step-390356. They show no 262K eval.
- Not fixed: the final save does not wait for pruning, so a temporary checkpoint can stay partly deleted. Restore takes the newer permanent checkpoint.

commits.author: hrl20
commits.message: [ci] Install only Playwright's headless shell for the Iris smoke test (#11013) Install only Playwright's Chromium headless shell in iris-e2e-smoke, without `--with-deps`. Every library Chromium needs is already on the ubuntu-24.04 image, so `--with-deps` only apt-installed Playwright's font packages (21.1 MB). On some runners the Azure Ubuntu mirror serves those at about 48 kB/s, so the install takes 7 to 9 minutes and the job hits its 10-minute timeout while the smoke tests run: | Run | Install step | Result | |---|---|---| | [42113791909, attempt 2](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/actions/runs/42113791909/job/127566704645) | 7 min 52 s | cancelled at timeout | | [42148823852](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/actions/runs/42148823852/job/127667012083) | 7 min 38 s | cancelled at timeout, tests 78% done and passing | | [42154488182](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/actions/runs/42154488182/job/127685543355) | 8 min 50 s | cancelled at timeout | On a fast mirror the same step takes 18 s ([42113791909, attempt 3](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/actions/runs/42113791909/job/127584546739)). The tests launch Chromium headless, which uses the headless shell, and they compare no screenshots, so the fonts only change how non-Latin glyphs look in the uploaded screenshots. `--only-shell` alone doesn't help: `--with-deps` always adds Playwright's tools group, and on Ubuntu 24.04 that group is the font packages. Also add `unified-unit.yaml` to the suite's triggers, as the other isolated suites have, so a change to the job runs it. That includes this PR.

commits.author: yonromai
commits.message:
[ci] Reduce checkout downloads in six workflows (#11018)

Reduce Git downloads in six CI jobs. Four jobs use blobless checkouts:
they keep commit history and fetch file contents as needed. The two
dependency updaters use shallow checkouts because they need only the
latest source files.

Local measurements at `26b6d560d4e9`:

| Checkout | Git directory | Fetch and checkout |
|---|---:|---:|
| Full history and file contents | 1,036 MB | 42.9 s |
| Blobless history | 80 MB | 11.1 s |
| Latest commit only | 30 MB | 3.9 s |

Historical source reads brought the blobless checkout to 91 MB. The
shallow checkout stayed at 30 MB after refreshing `main`.

Full and optimized checkouts produced matching job selections, release
plans, reports and historical source files. Updater checks in disposable
repositories confirmed that stale pushes cannot overwrite concurrent
updates. A job submission dry run also produced matching inputs. All 87
focused tests passed; PR CI finished with 26 passing and 25 skipped
checks.

Co-authored-by: Romain Yon <1596570+yonromai@users.noreply.github.com>

commits.author: asartran
commits.message:
[ci] Clone without historical file contents in the unit test selector (#11004)

Makes the first job of the "Marin - Unit" check download about 75 MB
instead of about 1 GB, so every unit-test run starts its tests roughly
25 seconds sooner.

Every job in the unit-test workflow waits for the `select` job, which
decides which tests to run from the PR's diff. That job cloned the full
repository history including every past version of every file, about 1
GB. In sampled runs from Oct 13 to Nov 5, its checkout step took a
median of 32 s, 47 s at p90, and up to 316 s.

The selector needs every commit to find the merge base and list the
changed files, but file contents only for the checked-out tree. The
checkout now uses a partial clone (`filter: blob:none`), which downloads
commits and directory listings but no historical file contents. Git
fetches any other file the selector reads, such as the base `uv.lock`
for the TPU dependency check, on demand.

On a GitHub runner, "before" is the median of 478 sampled runs from Oct
13 to Nov 5 and "after" is this change's CI run
([job](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/actions/runs/42137901055)):

| `select` job on GitHub `ubuntu-latest` | Before (p50) | After | Change
|
|---|---|---|---|
| Checkout step | 32 s | 7 s | -25 s |
| Whole job | 38 s | 11 s | -27 s |

From a development machine, a full clone took 54 s and 983 MB of `.git`;
the partial clone took 9 s and 74 MB. The selector ran unchanged on the
partial clone, including the TPU dependency check that reads the base
`uv.lock`.

Co-authored-by: Amy Sartran <users.noreply.github.com>

and run its vLLM arms nightly. A workflow matrix submits one CPU root
per cluster: H100 pp1/pp2 on CoreWeave and TPU v4 on Marin. Iris
federates whole roots, so each test's accelerator children stay with
their parent. The Levanter arm remains unchanged and runnable manually.
Delete the separate serving-parity launcher and runner; retain their
live-code contract tests beside the existing cluster tests.

The TPU request uses four coscheduled hosts, forwards the requested
per-host CPU allocation to Ray, and keeps the existing probability bound
and exact same-process repeatability checks. The verified June d819
export is now durable at
`gs://marin-us-central2/models/snowball/june-67b-a2b-step-42150/d819cbc63780bd866a942e47f9283cbd7932bbb237b52df527edd750c65be8f0/`.

134,175,089,690 bytes), preserving the original streamed source hashes;
its manifest is published last.

shutdown policies. Each leg exposes its own final result and
resource-exhaustion flag and marks resource exhaustion as failure in its
last step. Slack skips only when every failing leg is a capacity

Eight cases check the actual Slack condition. Required lint/type checks
and advisory review are clean. Live pytest-parent validation:

Pytest wall |

| v4-32 TP16 | `5de9734cee` |64/64|0.061427|pass|1270.37s|

Errors are rounded from child logs. Both tests passed without skips;

[rl] Publish assessments with a small share of unavailable judgments (#10919)

FULL campaigns on the structure-closure validation cohort could not pass
grading: GLM serialized `evidence_ids` as the array's bare body
(brackets and edge quotes dropped) on adversarial packets, and a
reviewer answered an ID-mismatch trap. Two of 105 judgments were
unparseable, and any unavailable judgment failed the campaign, the
catalog publish, and the Atlas load alike.

Judgment parsing now repairs stringified `evidence_ids` arrays and

stay recorded as unavailable judgments with their raw text; campaign,
publish, and load fail only when the unavailable share exceeds
`MAX_UNAVAILABLE_JUDGMENT_SHARE` (2%).

revalidate under the repaired parser without new inference.

commits.author: loom-oa-dev[bot]
commits.message:
[grug] Read Hero length buckets from existing token caches (#10980)

The Hero's 262K extension can train on documents above 65,536 tokens at
4× the sampling weight of shorter documents. The loader reads the
Harrier token caches and writes no token data. A second store split by
document length uses too much CoreWeave space.

Selection:

- `launch_scaling_ladder.py` selects the mix from context length: a Hero
above `LONG_CONTEXT_THRESHOLD` reads it.
- `launch_diagnostics.py --long-context-start-step N` selects the mix
for diagnostic arms. An `N` above 0 requires `--restore-from`.
- At the 65,536 tokens on `main`, the Hero reads Harrier. Its built
config matches `main` except for a null `data.mixture_start_step` field.

Sampling:

- Each cooldown cell becomes one short stream and one long stream. Each
stream holds its tokens once and has its own shuffle. The two weights of
a cell sum to its cooldown weight.
- At 4×, the weights give long documents 43.9% of tokens, against 22.2%
at 1×. The 8× treatment in #8813 gave 43.4%, against 14.9% at 1×.
- `MixtureDataset` truncates block counts, which gives 43.7%. The
remainder, 199 of 49,152 sequences, goes to `c30q4/short`.
`c00q0/short`, `c13q0/short` and 43 long buckets get no sequences. These
long buckets hold 7.4B of 5.36T long tokens.
- Over 200B tokens, long documents get 0.016 passes overall. The worst
bucket, `c12q1/long`, gets 0.16 passes.

Start position:

- `LmDataConfig.mixture_start_step` makes a selected step read the first
sequence of the mixture. A later restore continues in place. A restore
before the start raises an error.

Length statistics:

- A Zephyr step reads document offsets and writes one 17 MB file.
- The loader uses the file to set sampling weights and to find
documents. The skew is not an input to the scan.
- Its totals match the ledgers and `available_tokens` for all 200 cells.

Other changes:

- Every Grug trainer calls `LmDataConfig.train_mixture`, because
`train_sets` returns one source for each bucket.
- `MixtureDataset` raises an error when a source with positive weight is
missing.
- `DataLoader` reads its example from the first readable index of the
dataset, so a mixture can start past index 0.

Training runs:

- The one-rack semifinal and the 11-rack test ran this mix at 8×.
- A one-rack keep166 arm at 4× (commit 61a2a9e674 on `hero-semifinal`)
is about to run. No GPU result exists at 4× yet.

Remaining work:

- The deploy PR must set the 262K context and append the 65,536-token
phase that ends at step 390251 to `HERO_CONTEXT_PHASES`.

Supersedes #10930. Part of #8435.

commits.author: mcwitt
commits.message:
[grug] Keep weights on their devices on the dropless eval move (#10994)

Keep each weight shard on its device when the hero moves weights to the
dropless eval mesh. At training `data` size 1, the move renames each
PartitionSpec: `expert` becomes `data`, and training `data` drops out.
At a larger training `data`, the move does not change.

- Cause: the unrenamed expert specs described a different layout on the
eval mesh, so the move ran a collective on a new 16-rank NCCL
communicator. The communicator's buffers stay outside the allocator pool
for the life of the process.
- Failure: at 262K, CP4 x EP16, capacity factor 1.5 on one rack, the
move raised rank 0 non-pool memory from 47.50 to 53.37 GiB. NCCL logged
5.63 GiB of new buffers during the move. The next train step was 1.62
GiB short and failed to allocate its 95.42 GiB arena.
- Earlier work: #10709 had this rename. #10877 replaced #10709,
reordered the mesh and left out the rename as unnecessary. Its 262K A/B
did not hit this OOM. This change adds the rename to the #10877 mesh.
- One-rack proof: `eval-oom-fix2` (ac8f0703aa, same move code as this
head) ran two eval-then-train cycles and a final eval. Rank 0 non-pool
memory stayed at 47.50 GiB. `eval-oom-fix1` (07f72869c6, same rename)
ran three cycles and logged no new communicator after the first train
step.
- Remaining copy: on multi-process runs, the move may still copy the
weights. Rack runs used 35 GiB more pool memory during each eval, then
freed it.
- 11-rack proof: `eval-oom-11rackp` (e8e58b910d, same move code) ran 100
steps with two handoffs, saves and a final eval. The move added no
non-pool memory on any of the 704 devices. The first eval forward made a
new 176-rank communicator, which used about 1.03 GiB on each device.
Later evals added none. The tightest device kept 2.08 GiB free.

[filer] Improve storage browsing and file previews (#11009)

Filer records successful location changes in browser history, including
pasted storage URLs. It copies stable Filer links and saves favorites
per verified Marina user. Folder listings offer list and grid views with
lazy image thumbnails. Selecting a text, Markdown, JSON, or code file
keeps the folder visible and opens a bounded source preview beside it,
with actions to copy either link or open the full file view.

Image and media previews render again. The Vue template previously tried
to construct `URLSearchParams`, which failed at runtime. The Parquet
schema view shows footer statistics and supports a direct row jump
without reading earlier row groups.

Agent guidance pairs storage URLs with Filer links for browser readers.
The favorites migration adds one table to Filer's app schema. Thumbnails
are limited to 1 MiB per object; media previews remain limited to 10
MiB.

[iris] Delete duplicate controller and constraint tests (#10992)

Remove Iris tests that repeated another test's setup and assertions. The
direct-provider section of test_transitions.py duplicated
test_direct_controller.py: its pending-drain and redrive tests are
deleted, and its retry, worker-failure, cancel and sibling-kill tests
move into test_direct_controller.py, with its two overlapping
promotion-cap tests folded into one. The shared submit_direct_job helper
gains retry-limit arguments so the moved tests need no private submit
helper. Single duplicates are also removed from the bundle store,
service, auth, demand routing, dashboard, attempt count, CLI job, pod
manifest and worker reconcile tests, along with the constraint merge and
placement tests in test_types.py that test_constraints.py already runs.

Every assertion from a removed test is still checked by a surviving
test, for example test_drain_redrives_assigned_null_worker and
test_drain_executing_goes_to_running_tasks for the redrive test,
test_endpoint_token_carries_audience and test_cidr_only_outcomes for the
auth tests, and test_merge_canonical_key_child_overrides_parent for the
merge-override tests. Where a duplicate had one extra check, it moved
into the surviving test: the attempt row's ASSIGNED state, the task's
RUNNING state, the exit code and finish time after success, and the
values kept when merging non-canonical keys. test_constraints.py gains
canonical-override rows for region, preemptible and zone and an EQ zone
row in its placement table.

commits.message:
[ci] Run only the affected area's tests for experiment config changes (#10995)

Stops edits to experiment READMEs, launch configs and other non-Python
files under `experiments/` from running the whole marin unit-test suite,
so those PRs only run the tests that can read the changed file.

The CI test selector picks tests from a PR's diff by following Python
imports. A non-Python file cannot be traced that way, so the selector
treats any non-Python file in a test directory as a possible test
fixture and runs that package's full suite. Since all of `experiments/`
became a marin test directory (#9091), a README, YAML launch config,
shell script or prompt JSON there runs all 282 marin test files on three
runners. Between Oct 13 and Nov 5 this happened on 44 commits to main,
about 1 in 9, and on about a third of a sample of 35 recent PRs.

A non-Python file under `experiments/<area>/` now selects three groups
of tests:

- every test under that same top-level area;
- tests anywhere that import one of the area's Python modules (for
example `tests/datakit/test_hero_data.py`, which checks
`experiments/datakit/hero_data_paths.json` through
`experiments.datakit.hero_data`);
- tests whose source names the area as `experiments/<area>` or
`"experiments" / "<area>"` (for example
`tests/evaluation/test_evaluation.py`, which reads configs from
`experiments/evaluation/configs/`).

The area is the narrowest unit that covers how existing tests read such
files: a `fixtures/` folder beside the test, `../datasets`, and campaign
configs several folders below the test. An experiment `README.md`
selects no tests, since no test reads one. Files directly in
`experiments/`, `conftest.py`, test helpers and deleted modules keep the
full-suite rule.

To check the effect, the old and new selector were run on all 44
commits. Run times are estimates: each runner costs about 50 s of setup
plus about 2.5 s per test file, which matches the 285 s that a 94-file
marin runner took in the CI run of #10979. Test files vary widely in
cost, so treat the times as rough.

| Per affected commit | Before (p50) | After (p50) | After (p90) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Marin test files selected | 282 | 32 | 221 |
| Slowest marin runner | ~285 s (4.8 min) | ~99 s (1.6 min) | ~235 s
(3.9 min) |
| Total marin runner time | ~855 s (14.3 min) | ~180 s (3.0 min) | ~700
s (11.7 min) |

The slowest runner sets how long a PR waits only when marin finishes
last; evaluation-area changes still wait for the 6-8 minute Evalchemy
job. The same commits, grouped by how many tests they now select:

| Selection with this change | Commits | Marin test files (median) |
Runners | Est. runner time per commit | Est. slowest runner |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Before this change (all 44) | 44 | 282 | 3 | ~14 min | ~4.8 min |
| No tests (README only) | 3 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| 1-15 files | 10 | 6 | 1 | ~1 min | ~1 min |
| 16-60 files | 14 | 32 | 1-3 | ~3 min | ~1.6 min |
| 61-223 files | 13 | 67 | 3 | ~5.3 min | ~1.8 min |
| Full suite, unchanged | 4 | 282 | 3 | ~14 min | ~4.8 min |

In total, the 44 commits drop from about 627 to about 205 estimated
runner-minutes (-67%). The 4 commits that still run the full suite also
change a `conftest.py`, a test helper or a deleted module. Grug-area
changes will take longer than the table suggests, because grug tests
take 20-43 s each.
